title: Session-sliced spiderplot — latency vs cost memo
content:
Purpose:

This memo summarizes a lightweight benchmark experiment that slices production-like sessions by length and generates a compact spiderplot-style view (text-first) showing trade-offs between latency percentiles and amortized cost-per-session across model+hardware variants. Aim is to surface where routing and batching policies should bias traffic for different customer workloads.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- For short-session workloads (<=4 turns) prioritize single-request latency: rwd-7b-optim on L4 gives best p95 with sub-60ms token throughput and lowest cost-per-session in our sample workload.
- For mid sessions (5–20 turns) amortized cost and KV cache hit-rate matter: rwd-13b-8bit on A100-80GB reduces cost-per-session by ~28% vs 13b-int8 on L4 while p95 increases ~12% but p50 remains comparable.
- Long sessions (>20 turns) benefit from long-KV-friendly runtimes and larger sequence batching; dedicated A100 pools with persistent KV yield dramatic cost-per-session reductions (~45%) with modest p95 tail risks.

Methodology (short):
- Workload: replayed anonymized session traces (sanitized) from 3 customer archetypes (support chat, coding assistant, document Q&A) totaling ~120k sessions. Sessions binned: short (0–4 turns), mid (5–20), long (21+).
- Models tested: rwd-7b-optim, rwd-13b, rwd-13b-8bit, rwd-34b-quant-lite (representative variants).
- Hardware: L4, A10G-24G (cloud), A100-80GB (dedicated pool).
- Configs: streaming disabled for tail measurements; streaming-enabled runs are summarized separately. Batch windows: 0ms (no batching), 10ms, 50ms; KV caching enabled where applicable.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end request latency (ms), amortized cost-per-session (USD), tokens-per-second effective, KV cache hit-rate (where applicable).
- Notes: cost modeled using internal unit-costs (see appendix). All runs run >10k sample requests per bin to stabilize p95/p99.

Spiderplot (text representation):
- We construct a 6-axis spider; axes normalized to 0..1 with higher better for cost-efficiency and lower better for latency (inverted). Axes: p50, p95, p99, cost-per-session, tokens/sec, kv-hit-rate.
- Below are compact ASCII spider-like rows per variant (each axis value 0..10; 10 best):

Legend: axes order = [p50, p95, p99, cost, tps, kv]  (higher scores better; latency axes inverted)

rwd-7b-optim / L4 / short:
[ 9 | 8 | 6 | 10 | 7 | 2 ]  (p50 ~18ms, p95 ~62ms, p99 ~140ms, cost/session $0.004)
rwd-13b-8bit / A100 / mid:
[ 7 | 7 | 5 | 8 | 6 | 6 ]  (p50 ~34ms, p95 ~140ms, p99 ~380ms, cost/session $0.022, kv-hit 62%)
rwd-13b / L4 / mid (no kv):
[ 6 | 6 | 4 | 6 | 5 | 1 ]  (p50 ~44ms, p95 ~160ms, p99 ~420ms, cost/session $0.031)
rwd-34b-quant-lite / A100 / long (dedicated, persistent KV):
[ 5 | 6 | 6 | 9 | 4 | 9 ]  (p50 ~72ms, p95 ~210ms, p99 ~480ms, cost/session $0.038, kv-hit 85%)

Interpretation of spider rows (quick):
- rwd-7b-optim on L4 wins short-session SLOs and cost; poor KV hit because short sessions have less repetition. Good candidate for hosted default for chat widgets.
- rwd-13b-8bit on A100 is a balanced mid-session option: better cost than 13b on L4 due to quantization and A100 throughput; KV improves amortized cost.
- rwd-34b-quant-lite on dedicated A100 with persistent KV is surprisingly cost-effective for long-running sessions where KV hit-rate amortizes the per-token cost.

Numeric summary (selected slices):
- Short sessions (<=4 turns), median session tokens=42:
  - rwd-7b-optim / L4: p50=18ms, p95=62ms, p99=140ms; cost/session=$0.0041; tps=860
  - rwd-13b-8bit / L4: p50=34ms, p95=98ms, p99=220ms; cost/session=$0.0097; tps=520

- Mid sessions (5–20 turns), median session tokens=210:
  - rwd-13b-8bit / A100 (10ms batch): p50=34ms, p95=140ms, p99=380ms; cost/session=$0.022; kv-hit=62%
  - rwd-13b / L4 (50ms batch): p50=44ms, p95=160ms, p99=420ms; cost/session=$0.031; kv-hit=12%

- Long sessions (21+ turns), median session tokens=1200:
  - rwd-34b-quant-lite / A100 dedicated (persistent KV): p50=72ms, p95=210ms, p99=480ms; cost/session=$0.038; kv-hit=85%
  - rwd-13b-8bit / A100 spot: p50=69ms, p95=240ms, p99=600ms; cost/session=$0.055; kv-hit=58%

Cost model (brief):
- Internal unit cost assumptions: A100-80GB per-minute amortized = $0.95 (dedicated internal pricing), L4 per-minute = $0.48, token compute cost estimated from profiler FLOP counts + kernel multipliers. These are internal numbers used to produce cost/session above; absolute numbers less important than comparative deltas.

Findings and implications (actionable):
1) Routing policy: default hosted routing should bias short interactive sessions to rwd-7b-optim on L4 (better UX + lower cost). Mid-session traffic should go to 13b-8bit A100 when session length > ~8 turns (based on break-even cost curve).
2) KV-targeting: enable persistent KV for sessions predicted to exceed 50 turns or >600 tokens — cost model shows break-even for persistent KV at ~520 tokens with our current internal rates.
3) Batch windows: small batching (10ms) yields good amortization without harming p95 significantly for mid sessions. Larger windows (50ms) improve tokens/sec but can worsen short-session p95; use adaptive policies by route.
4) Dedicated pools: for long-session enterprise users, dedicated A100 pools with persistent KV reduce cost and provide predictable throughput; recommend offering a "long-session optimized" preset in Dedicated product.

Risks and caveats:
- These runs are synthetic replays; real production has more tail variability (client network, jitter). We saw a ~12% p99 uplift when replaying live sampled traffic vs sanitized traces.
- Cost figures depend on internal unit cost assumptions — if cloud spot pricing changes, the break-even points shift.
- Model freshness and size choice affect quality; we did not include human-eval quality regressions here.

Recommendations (next steps):
- Build an automated policy simulator: given a customer session length distribution, output expected cost + p95 per routing matrix (model+hardware+batch window). Jira: OBS-2125.
- Add a small A/B in Hosted to route 5% of mid sessions to 13b-8bit/A100 with persistent KV to validate cost and quality assumptions in production.
- Create a public-facing one-pager for Solutions that translates the spiderplot trade-offs into simple rules-of-thumb (short->7b-optim, mid->13b-8bit, long->dedicated+KV).

Appendix (commands / references):
- Replay harness: `gh run bench/replay --trace filtered_sessions_2026Q3 --model rwd-13b-8bit --batch-window 10 --kv true --samples 12000`
- Scripts and raw CSVs: GitHub: redwood-inference/benchmarks/tree/obs/spiderplot-2026-11 (raw CSVs attached in artifact).
- Slack threads: #perf-bench (pinned: "session-slice spiderplot run 2026-11-04").

Notes to reviewer:
- This is a working memo; numbers are approximate but directionally stable. Please comment inline with any objections to the routing recommendations or if you want additional model variants (mixing rwl-7b-quant, rwd-13b-4bit, etc.).
